definitions.gloss: burglary of an empty house; sneak thief; prowler
definitions.explanation: Breaking into and stealing from a house or building while the occupants are away. Also refers to the person who commits this crime.

examples.japanese: {空|あ}き{巣|す}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}られた→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{空|あ}き{巣|す}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{被害|ひがい}→被害：02572_higai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Burglaries have been increasing in this area.

examples.japanese: ⟦{旅行中|りょこうちゅう}→旅行中：28581_ryokouchuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{空|あ}き{巣|す}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}られない→入る：00494_hairu⟧よう、⟦{戸締|とじ}まり→戸締まり：17821_tojimari⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}した→確認する：25332_kakuninsuru⟧。
examples.english: I checked the locks to make sure we wouldn't be burgled while traveling.

notes:
USAGE:
Can refer to both the act of burglary and the burglar themselves. The key nuance is that the crime targets an empty dwelling—the occupants are not home.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {空|あ}き{巣|す}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}られる→入る：00494_hairu⟧ (to be burgled)
- {空|あ}き{巣|す}⟦{被害|ひがい}→被害：02572_higai⟧ (burglary damage)
- {空|あ}き{巣|す}⟦{対策|たいさく}→対策：02511_taisaku⟧ (anti-burglary measures)
- {空|あ}き{巣|す}⟦{狙|ねら}い→狙い：00312_nerai⟧ (targeting empty houses)

FORMS:
⟦{空|あ}き→空く：11062_aku⟧ (empty, vacant) + ⟦{巣|す}→巣：02140_su⟧ (nest, den). Literally "empty nest," referring to a home left unoccupied.
